Guide · Mozambique

Mozambique’s 50 m partial protection zone, explained

Mozambique’s Land Law makes a strip of 50 m on each side of pipelines, power lines and other conduits a partial protection zone, where no land-use right can be acquired. This guide sets out what the law says, how the petroleum and electricity laws build on it, what the draft reform would change, and what it means for an operator keeping the strip clear. A summary of public rules as of 26 September 2026; it is not legal advice.

Published 26 September 2026 · 5 min read

Written for: Oil & gas · Power & utilities · LNG, mining and large projects

Request a proposal Pipelines in Mozambique

What the Land Law says

The Land Law, Lei n.º 19/97, de 1 de Outubro, divides the public domain into total and partial protection zones. Article 8 lists the partial protection zones (zonas de protecção parcial, ZPP). For linear infrastructure, the key item is article 8(g): the land occupied by motorways and four-lane roads, and by instalações e condutores aéreos, superficiais, subterrâneos e submarinos de electricidade, de telecomunicações, petróleo, gás e água, com uma faixa confinante de 50 metros de cada lado: overhead, surface, underground and submarine installations and conduits for electricity, telecommunications, oil, gas and water, with an adjoining strip of 50 m on each side.

The same article sets other strips that matter to land-holding companies:

Article 8 Partial protection zone
(c) 100 m of land along the coast
(d) 100 m around springs
(e) 250 m around dams and reservoirs
(f) Railways, with 50 m on each side of the axis
(g) Oil, gas, water, electricity and telecommunications installations and conduits, with 50 m on each side; roads, with 30 m for primary and 15 m for secondary and tertiary roads
(h) 2 km along the land border
(i) Airports and aerodromes, with a 100 m strip
(j) Military and other defence and security installations, with a 100 m strip

What the zone means

Protection zones are public domain (art. 6). No land-use right (DUAT) can be acquired in them; the law allows only special licences, licenças especiais, for specific activities (art. 9). A DUAT cannot therefore be the basis for building inside the 50 m strip, and anything that stands there sits on public-domain land.

That does not make each structure in the strip a simple case. Some predate the infrastructure, and some have special licences. The strip tells an operator where the law protects the line; it does not settle, by itself, what happens to what already stands there.

How the sector laws build on it

Petroleum. The Petroleum Law of June 2026 repeats the strip for petroleum infrastructure: as áreas que circundam as infra-estruturas numa faixa de 50 metros, consideram-se zonas de protecção parcial (Lei n.º 8/2026, art. 75(3)). It leaves the safety zone to regulation (75(4)), provides compensation for damage to crops, buildings and improvements (75(5)) and allows rights of passage (75(7)). The rights holder bears resettlement costs after prior consultation (art. 61).

The Pande–Temane corridor. Decreto n.º 36/2001, de 20 de Novembro sets a 50 m partial protection zone (art. 1) and a 200 m safety zone (art. 2) on each side of the Pande–Temane gas pipeline corridor and around its processing and compression unit, and requires the project operator’s prior consent for infrastructure there (art. 3). It was made under the petroleum law of the time; whether it continues unchanged under the regulation the 2026 law calls for is a point to confirm with counsel.

Electricity. The Electricity Law sets an administrative servitude of até 50 metros confinantes … contados a partir do eixo da linha: up to 50 m, counted from the line’s axis, recorded on the concession (Lei n.º 12/2022, art. 43(4)). The width depends on voltage and setting (43(5)), a safety zone lies inside it (43(6)), and the servitude is registered in the Cadastro de Terras and the Conservatória do Registo Predial (43(7)). Resettlement and compensation rules apply (43(8)), but no compensation is owed where the holders or owners acquired their rights after the line was built (43(10)).

Two ways of counting

The Land Law describes a strip on each side of the installation; the Electricity Law counts from the line’s axis. For a buried pipeline and an overhead line, those can be different lines on the ground. Which one a given width is measured from is a question for your counsel and your concession terms.

What the draft reform would change

The Council of Ministers approved a Land Law proposal for submission to the Assembleia da República on 28 October 2025 (AIM). The published June 2024 draft (ante-projecto, art. 15(3)):

  • keeps the 50 m strip for conduits;
  • widens the coastal strip to 200 m and the strip around springs to 150 m, and sets roads at 30 m and 15 m on each side;
  • keeps 100 m around airports and military installations, and adds 250 m around military servitudes;
  • would let the distances, including the conduit strip, be reduced or increased (art. 15(4)).

Until the Assembleia adopts a text, Lei n.º 19/97 is the law in force. Check the adopted text before relying on any new width.

What it means for an operator

Know what stands in the strip. A register of the structures inside the 50 m zone and in a band outside it, each measured to the line, tells the servitude team where the strip is clear, where it is filling and which stretches to visit first.

Record the date. The Electricity Law turns compensation on when rights were acquired, and the Petroleum Law provides compensation for damage in the zone. A register tied to dated imagery, compared with earlier imagery where it exists, is the record those questions come back to.

Plan regularisation and resettlement on facts. Where structures must move, resettlement follows Decreto n.º 31/2012 and, on lender-funded projects, IFC Performance Standard 5. A dated register sizes the census and shows what arrived after the cut-off date: see resettlement cut-off-date baselines.

Route new lines around the land. For a new pipeline or line, counting the structures along each option within the same strips weighs the land affected before the route is fixed.

How AfriScan measures the strip

We buffer the route you supply in its UTM zone, so distances are in true metres, and report structures within 50 m and 100 m by default. We add the 200 m safety zone where it applies, or any width from your concession, servitude or safety study, up to six in one survey. Each structure comes with its distance to the line, its band, its chainage and its coordinates; each 500 m of route is rated for encroachment density; and a person reviews every result before delivery, in Portuguese or English.

Our registers are not cadastral surveys: DUAT demarcation is the work of the land cadastre services and sworn surveyors. We do not decide whether a structure is authorised or who is owed compensation.

Frequently asked questions

Is the 50 m counted from the pipe or from the edge of the servitude?

The Land Law describes a strip of 50 m on each side of the installations and conduits (art. 8(g)); the Electricity Law counts its servitude from the line’s axis (art. 43(4)). Which line a width is measured from is a question for your counsel and your concession terms. Our registers measure from the line in the route file you supply, so tell us what that line is and we set the bands to match.

Can anyone obtain a DUAT inside the zone?

No. Land-use rights cannot be acquired in partial protection zones; the law allows only special licences for specific activities there (Lei n.º 19/97, art. 9).

Are the houses already inside the zone unlawful?

That is not for a mapping company to decide. Some structures predate the line, special licences can exist, and the sector laws provide compensation and resettlement where people must move. A register records what stands where, and when; your land team and the authorities decide its status.

Will the new Land Law change the 50 m strip?

The June 2024 draft keeps the 50 m strip for conduits but would allow the widths to be reduced or increased (art. 15(4)). The Council of Ministers approved a Land Law proposal on 28 October 2025; check the text the Assembleia da República adopts before relying on any width.

Know what stands inside your 50 m strip.

Send the route or line and the widths that apply: 50 m, 100 m, the 200 m Pande–Temane safety zone or your concession's. We reply with a scope and a written proposal.
